A connected way
to make things happen.

An idea does not move in a straight line. A sample changes the brief. A customer changes the offer. A return improves the next design.

Start wherever
the opportunity is.

A maker can start with spare capacity. A community can start with a shared need. Someone else can start with a material looking for a new use.

The steps below are a useful route through the work. They are not ranks, gates controlled by a central authority, or a compulsory sequence.

Agree the work, together.

Record the contribution, the people involved, its terms and its limits. A responsibility lasts for the agreed activity. It does not become permanent standing over others.

AI-generated concept artwork. Samples and connected making.
01

Find the intention

Describe who the product is for and the experience it should support. A sketch, conversation or existing object can be enough to begin.

What comes out: A brief that another person can understand.

02

Make and learn

Prepare a sample. Try it in the real setting. Keep observations about fit, flavour, comfort, use and care attached to the version tested.

What comes out: A sample record and a clear next revision.

03

Connect the means

Bring together materials, artwork, makers and quotations. Compare the same specification, quantities and delivery terms.

What comes out: An agreed specification, contributions and dated costs.

04

Shape the offer

Explain exactly what someone receives, the price, variants, timing and handover. Keep a single item, a refill and a collection as distinct offers.

What comes out: An understandable offer and a fulfilment plan.

05

Share the experience

Use the product, tell its story and invite feedback. People choose their participation, and creators agree how their work is used.

What comes out: Release material, customer questions and useful feedback.

06

Follow the next use

Record repairs, returns, refills and recovery with a real receiving route. Bring costs, losses and experience into the next design.

What comes out: A completed movement and learning for the next cycle.

One record.
Many useful views.

A product connects with its material, pattern, maker, offer and feedback. A project can connect to several products. There is no required parent project.

A revised fabric should reach the maker’s brief, costs and product description. The working edition lets you keep that information together and export a portable pack.

Live synchronisation between businesses, stock systems and AI services is part of the wider design.
